artists.biography:
EMF are an alternative dance band from England. The band, from the Forest of Dean in Gloucestershire, came to prominence at the beginning of the 1990s. During its initial eight-year run (1989–1997), EMF had released three studio albums and had gone on hiatus and reformed twice. Their first single, "Unbelievable," reached number 3 in the UK Singles Chart, and was a number one hit on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart. Their debut album, Schubert Dip, went to number 3 in the UK Albums Chart.

The band was signed by EMI/Parlophone after four concerts, without even being asked for a demo tape.

perplexity.description:
Schubert Dip is the debut album by British dance-rock quintet EMF, released on Parlophone Records on May 7, 1991. The album showcases the band's fusion of rock instrumentation with electronic and techno elements, a sound the group developed after incorporating a Casio sampler and sequencer into their initially rock-oriented approach. Comprising 10 songs across 44 minutes, the album established EMF's signature infectious, dance-oriented rock style that would define their early career.

The album achieved substantial commercial success, reaching number 3 on the UK charts and number 12 in the US, while finishing 1991 at number 57 overall. Most significantly, it was certified platinum in the US by September 1991, indicating over a million copies sold. The album's lead single, "Unbelievable," became a major international hit, reaching number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 3 in the UK, establishing the band as a prominent force in early 1990s pop and rock.

As EMF's only debut, Schubert Dip remains their most commercially successful and culturally significant release, capturing the band at their commercial peak and establishing the template for their subsequent work throughout the 1990s.
